decisions.reason: The charting bundle extends the core map.apps platform the firm knows well, and its rapid early releases show the firm can learn from use and keep improving it at low cost, even though it no longer appears on the website.

The hierarchical search bundle draws on established map.apps search knowledge and is cheap to maintain, but its absence from the website since 2020 suggests it may be merged into general search functionality.

VueTOC rests on the firm's mobile web mapping expertise, but as an experimental component not seen since 2020 it is a likely candidate to be absorbed into newer products, so withdrawal is a real risk.
Mobile field data capture lies close to the firm's GIS competence and serves both public and private customers, so its knowledge base supports keeping it despite its lower website visibility.
The search extension complements the firm's web map apps using knowledge the firm already holds, so keeping it costs little, though it could be consolidated with other search components.
